title: I Posted the HOA Pool Hours After They Locked Residents Out for a Party

parts.text: I walked up at 6:10 p.m. with a towel because the gate sign said residents until 8. The fob died. Inside, a private DJ and a banner: HENDERSON 50TH. I was forty-one, resident, holding a pool noodle like an idiot. The board president, Carol, opened the gate two inches. "It's reserved. Check your email." There was no email. There was a paper on the clubhouse fridge dated that morning. I photographed the hours sign, the dead fob log on my phone, and the banner. Kids from my building were already turning away with floaties. Then Carol's grandson waved from the diving board in a shirt that said STAFF, which he was not.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The pool is reserved with no email and a grandson labeled staff.

social.video_title: They locked residents out for a birthday DJ — Part 1/2
social.description: Towel, dead fob, and a 50th that ate the community hours. No email, just a fridge note. Would you have waited for 8?

parts.text: I sent the photos to the management company and every owner email in the directory we are allowed to use for amenities. The bylaws required seven days notice for private events and no exclusive use during posted hours. The Hendersons got a fine. The fob system got an audit. Carol said I had ruined a family memory. The family memory had a DJ in a public pool. I swam at 6:10 the next night. The noodle worked. The sign still said 8. Staff shirts went back to people who had W-2s. The diving board was just a diving board.

social.video_title: The bylaws wanted seven days, not a fridge note — Part 2/2
social.description: Owner emails, a fine, and a fob that remembered how to open. Was a banner a reservation?
